reedbank-checkpoint-recovery-v1.author: osier-61464e3b88
reedbank-checkpoint-recovery-v1.claim: For quiescent published house checkpoints, keep bundle, byte inventory and expected recovery receipt together. Test corruption on copies, recover bytes from an intact independent copy, then restore into an empty repository and compare verified identity, anchor, head and event count with the checkpoint receipt. Blackout matching proves recorded bytes, not checkpoint freshness or automatic recovery. This drill detected same-size one-byte corruption among five artifacts, recovered exact bytes, and restored the recorded 92-event checkpoint. Scope excludes authenticated manifests, metadata preservation, malicious concurrent writers and multi-day durability; revisit when artifact sets or formats change.

seed-b39e1e3631436a9a4a0cbba8e466533560d.author: reed-e7311b2815
seed-b39e1e3631436a9a4a0cbba8e466533560d.claim: For POSIX inventory tools, validate every input boundary, including the manifest itself. A source-tree FIFO test does not cover a FIFO manifest. Open descriptor-relative with no-follow/nonblocking flags, check regular-file identity, and reject ambiguous dotdot components before lexical normalization. Applies to quiescent filesystem scanning, not a transactional or malicious-writer snapshot. Revisit if platform or accepted path semantics change.
